縫鎖，也須是個超絕佛祖底妙手。今日六月小盡，一年已瓜分半個去也。雞足山中飲光尊者作麼生思量？兜率天上逸多大士又如何計較？秪如壁上掛錢財；老鼠咬腰帶。者個消息也須透過，若透不過問取西樓笑長老。」師歸方丈，笑公隨進，師云：「如有人問長老：『壁上掛錢財；老鼠咬腰帶，是甚麼消息？』如何荅他？」笑曰：「直待禪床震動。」師云：「秪如天上無彌勒、地下無彌勒時，是誰禪床震動？」笑曰：「多煩和尚挂齒。」師云：「恁麼那？」笑曰：「誰敢擊雷門？」師微笑。小參：「菴提遮女問文殊：『明知生是不生之義，死是不死之義，如何又被生死之所流轉？』文殊云：『其力未充。』」杖人云：「當時只合扣齒三下。」「進山主亦以此義問修山主，修云：『筍畢竟成竹去，如今作篾用得麼？』進云：『老兄欠悟在。』」杖人云：「我只將一把稻草與他。」「修云：『老兄又作麼生？』進以手指云：『者個是監院房；者個是典座房。』修即禮拜。」杖人云：「我只震聲一喝。大眾！汝等若於此三轉語薦得，許你與古人各有出身活路；汝若不薦，且一坑埋卻。」天界覺浪盛禪師語錄卷五天界覺浪盛禪師語錄卷六門人大成大奇等編小參，舉：「雪庭裕和尚因僧參，庭問：『甚處人？』曰：『青州。』庭曰：『識得趙州布衫否？』曰：『趙州布衫近被人裂破了也。』庭曰：『因甚裂破？』曰：『風流不在著衣多。』庭便打。曰：『因甚打某甲？』

Occurrences.Kwic: 勉強作就，而衷心必抱愧怍，逢人說著，面負慚赧。世事尚然，況吾徒欲紹隆佛祖無上大道，寧不朝乾夕惕，直截根源？汝等勿謂戒法非直捷也。是故汝等若作戒受即不得，不作戒受亦不得。老僧今日不避口業，為汝等叨呾一上。汝等既發大心，求大乘戒，要將先聖遺訓兢兢佩服，如萬箭攢身，無處迴避，時時刻刻如渡得船，如病遇醫，疾不瘳，苦海未渡，不可輕放，方堪受戒。若少懷欺慢，于戒法中略有過犯，即落他因果矣。今時禪者幸有向上之志，奈何得少為足，認個無戒可受、無禪可參、無天堂可昇、無地獄可墮，佛法兩忘，人我齊遣，渾渾圇圇、瀟瀟灑灑，謂之解脫了事衲僧，即得望佛祖授受波羅提木叉，何啻白雲萬里？示禪者示禪者開峰禪道初無難易，秖要學者根志堅長，念念如救頭然，不作兒戲。參個僧問趙州：狗子還有佛性也無？州云：無。秖向日用尋常善惡逆順、動靜閒忙處提撕，不可固執偏邪、遏捺昏散以求成片，放教如長江大河滔流不息，忽然一念回機便見源底，久久純熟，自知源之與流非一非異，隨方自在、觸事活脫，應機利物、不守一隅，所謂取之無盡、用之不竭，實知有恁麼事，方得受用無礙。不然，則如說食終不濟饑。近時主方脈者未能越格變通，其病多在失候違時，誤人不少，或謂如一座須彌頓在面前搖撼不動。噫！是何言歟？佛祖出世本欲與人解粘去縛，安可將他無罪人妄上一重枷鎖？總之，自己曾未真實參悟，向冊子上東抄西錄，說得如花似錦，瞞無眼人年久月深，非不高大門墻聲馳譽走，爭奈生死到來不得自由，小著病苦便如蜘蛛上粉墻。今日已是惡日，不能收拾，一發盡情為汝等說破，不圖打艸，且要驚蛇。此一等人非是打頭無真志向，多緣宿昔業習深厚，一出頭來，冤家路狹，自無智眼，不覺被他抬動，打失正念，奔南走北，欣欣然認作福報。不知古人云：「道業未成，一切有為總是魔業。」是以諸大菩薩以本行德回向三有及佛菩提，出生入死，自不被他牽挽，豈似今時熱熱鬧鬧，逗到下場頭，恐懼切心，便去強作主宰，長時打坐？以圭峰散亂隨情轉，臨終被業牽，醒悟不由情，臨終能轉業之語以為公驗，每每向人道：定中殺有快活處。苦哉！胡不思七顛八倒那伽定耶？或者見人恁麼道，便乃隨情縱意，略不檢察，一朝老病到來，毫無效驗，便計較我死時心識畢竟昏懵，不能決眾，預先捏上幾句說話，撾鼓陞堂辭眾，及至臨期，卻又總死不成，遭人怪笑，疑慮後昆，反不如世間俗人卻無此等忌諱。然則一口氣不來時，畢竟有何旨訣？毘婆尸佛早留心，直至于今不得妙。參。示鑿池諸禪者示鑿池諸禪者佛法如水中月，清波無透路。雲門老人欲隱彌露，且問諸人：未開池時，月在何處？開池而後，月自何來？知未開池前月在何處，即知開池後月自何來。在處來處既知，則知自己腳跟下一段光明照耀天地，可謂鑿池非待月，池成月自來也。雖然，汝等諸人還知老僧落處麼？月落後來方丈，與你一碗茶喫。示映天飯頭示映天飯頭此事要在日用中著眼，看那個是我自己。若檢點得出，便具淘砂去米，淘米去砂，砂米齊去，覆卻飯盆底作略。開峰者裏又且不然，砂米齊去時，要見冷鍋中豆爆，冷甑上飯香，始堪咬嚼。示憨岳李居士示憨岳李居士在家人學道，盡謂鬧中取靜，豈知彼本欲了事，不可更為他多事去也。不見古人道：「火中生蓮終不壞。」者朵芬花豈容造作？蓋造作而成，終須變壞，安得為之終不壞耶？憨岳居士試向動容周旋時覷捕，看那個是不壞底火中蓮花，捕著時持來奉獻開峰拄杖子。職事榜職事榜自古叢林，為老病者設也。既為老病而設，則強壯無病者，未可輕居。必須知慚識愧，克苦勵精，以紹隆佛種為念，方不負十方檀施之厚德，一期化主之深心。凡我同袍，發好心，甘淡薄，欲同住者，隨所堪任，各效一職，務在真實，勿容虛偽。日用居常，互為主伴，遞相供養，容敬色莊，表裏瑩徹，如寶絲網，交光相羅，無混無礙，即所謂僧海珠也。如或躲懶偷安，坐視勞務，不憐老病，不事謙和，無道德號令人天，無行業取法後進，直一緇林鸇鴆焉也，非我手足。安禪榜安禪榜佛祖出世，本無實法與人；衲子安禪，入道豈有程限
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB428.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Mixingren. Mixing Jiren warns practitioners who have gathered polished sayings and public reputations that illness and death may still leave them helpless. He criticizes people who, frightened as death approaches, try forcibly to establish an inner controller and sit for long periods, using Guifeng Zongmi's verse as their warrant. The quoted first pair says that a distracted person follows feelings and is dragged along by past deeds at death; the following pair says that clear awakening does not follow feelings and can turn past deeds at death. Mixing then asks why such people fail to consider a settled freedom present even amid tumbling disorder. He also rejects the opposite response of indulging feelings without examination, and mocks rehearsed farewell speeches that do not enable a person to die as announced. The headword is Guifeng's quoted voice. Mixing's current teaching opposes both forced last-minute control and careless indulgence; it does not promise that performing a prescribed posture ensures a good death.

Linquan Conglun comments on a verse responding to a monk's exchange with Shoushan. After contrasting advance in search of reputation with turning back toward oneself, he quotes Guifeng: meaningful action belongs to an awakened mind, meaningless action to a scattered mind; distraction follows feelings and is dragged by past deeds at death, while awakening does not follow feelings and can turn those deeds. Linquan then urges withdrawing a step toward oneself and gathering body and mind, rather than pursuing fame and adding flaws. He compares the latter pursuit to Bian He's painful effort to have an uncut jade recognized, and prefers guarding one's own wish-fulfilling jewel. Here the death warning supports a present contrast between outward recognition and self-examination. Guifeng remains the exact quoted speaker; Linquan supplies this application within his current commentary, rather than giving instructions for arranging a death scene.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1403.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tianru Weize. In a reply to deputy Zhongwen's questions during illness, Tianru Weize first discusses freedom amid the eight kinds of suffering, saying that treating freedom as something outside suffering still leaves an opposition to overcome. The incoming question then quotes Guifeng's complete verse and asks whether even accomplished people arrange their seated or standing deaths; the writer, late to the path and still caught in feelings and past deeds, asks what he could rely on without awakening or some arrangement. Tianru replies that the matter at the boundary of life and death cannot be arranged only when the moment arrives. Inquiry and work beforehand are themselves preparation; after a breakthrough, he says, one settles old deeds as conditions allow and departs when worldly ties are exhausted, without having to manage it. Thus the quoted warning becomes a concrete ill person's question and a teacher's reply. The source's claims about realization and dying remain its teaching, not a guarantee of a chosen physical manner of death.

Huihong quotes Guifeng's daily-use verse, including the contrast between being dragged by past deeds and being able to turn them at death, then recalls a Tang historical account of Li Xun's flight. In Huihong's account, Guifeng wished to shelter Li; after Li was captured and killed, the official Qiu Shiliang questioned Guifeng. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB359.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baiyu. The question asks where the credit or merit belongs at a specifically described moment; its answer changes with the setting. At a New Year address, Baiyu Jingsi waves his whisk to either side and raises it while invoking the sage's appearance and a world in harmony: rulers and ministers at ease, the four seas peaceful, people flourishing, and rain and sun arriving in season. Asked where the merit belongs, he replies that thoughts could be counted, the ocean drunk dry, space measured and wind bound, yet the Buddha's virtues could not be exhausted in speech. The question redirects the grand scene toward immeasurable Buddha-merit rather than inviting a literal allocation of ceremonial credit among those present.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB453.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanjie Ying. When appointing the two ranks of monastery officers, Yuanjie Jingying emphasizes trustworthy colleagues who act as arms for one another, interchange guest and host, and match response with call. Together they are to renew the ancestral way. He then asks where credit belongs, draws the preserved signs in the air with his staff, and says there is no need to annotate them again: the line-images are clear of themselves. His response presents the working pattern through a gesture instead of naming an individual recipient of merit. The precise signs should not be expanded into a doctrinal chart the passage does not supply.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB468.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shanyi Chun. Shanyi Ruchun places the question after rejecting several ready-made accounts of realization. He demands the overturning of old nests and describes free application: a blade of grass becomes a towering Buddha and the Buddha a blade of grass; one may carry a bag through the marketplace or occupy a hut on a solitary peak. Asked where credit belongs at just this point, he strikes his staff and replies that the dragon sleeve sweeps open to reveal the whole, while where the elephant king walks no fox tracks remain. The question caps this account of unrestricted use with an emphatic display, rather than awarding personal achievement to a named teacher.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1404.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wu’an Puning. Wu'an Puning asks the question during a discourse requested by a high-ranking patron at the close of a prayer rite. He imagines great wisdom wielding bow and arrow over the whole world, subduing hostile forces until the realm is peaceful and tribute arrives from every direction. After asking where credit belongs, he pauses and says that without using even an inch of blade the demons' courage is broken and surrender flags are already raised at the mere sight of the approaching power. The martial answer turns on effectiveness without an actual stroke; it belongs to the discourse's ceremonial imagery, not a report of a battle fought at the monastery.

In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Feiyin, Feiyin Tongrong tells the assembly to open it here and see the Buddha amid red dust. Gulin Qingmao's verse calls it seven or eight catties on each side and says it is blind in an instant. These predicates keep one phrase in transmission wording and changing visual images rather than dividing it into separate objects.

Senses.Explanation: The phrase names what lineage narratives claim is possessed, entrusted, preserved, or destroyed in transmission. Shakyamuni Buddha says he possesses it and entrusts it to Mahakasyapa. Wumen Huikai turns that founding claim into a challenge by repeatedly asking how it could be transmitted. Buddhanandi entrusts it to his successor with an injunction not to let it be cut off. At death Linji Yixuan tells the assembly not to destroy his treasury; Sansheng Huiran replies that he would not dare, but after Sansheng's shout Linji says it will perish with this blind donkey. Another lamp passage again quotes Shakyamuni entrusting it to Mahakasyapa. The phrase is therefore an asserted lineage possession whose transmission is both ritually declared and sharply interrogated.

Senses.Explanation: The pivot that stamps the day at hand as the one point where the question lands — between two buddhas, or at the hinge of an occasion. Muchen Daomin, holding the unrestricted Avatamsaka assembly, sets the squeeze: Sakya has passed, Maitreya is yet to come — right this very day, who rules as lord inside the flower-treasury world? Zhe'an Jingfan works the same formula free of longing: Sakya gone, why chase the past; Maitreya unbuilt, why yearn ahead — right this very day, you with wits, breed no stray doubt, for the doubtless one is the hero. Yuanjie Jingying turns his own birthday: forty-four years before he dwelt in the past, after in the present — right this very day sage and ordinary interlace, host and guest converge, and no mark of same or different can be found; Chulin Shangrui rides the counting-nines rhyme over the ice to the enlightenment-day feast and asks what the feast is now — old Sakya's whole affair gone flat; Koho Kennichi, mid-summer, splits the season — first half an arrow off the string, second half a long sword propped on heaven — and right this very day asks who tops the school's measure; Guantao Daqi hands the new abbot the enthronement knife: right this very day the lives of all buddhas past and the founding teachers rest in the new elder's hand — release or hold, no one else decides; Yuan'an Liao at the winter release asks why the ninety days leaked no water, and what great gate swings wide right this very day; and Yushan Shangsi, at the requiem for a slaughtered-life karma, asks where the father is born — right this very day, what land after all?

He then places dust thick over a street, green water flowing beneath a bridge, winding song in a wine shop and relaxed laughter in a butcher's shop before the assembly. Since there is no indirectness, he says, there is naturally no doubt; he asks how the people present can take responsibility for this. Throwing down the staff, he closes with the accomplished person's broad view and fitting movement. Senses.Explanation: A time-freeze that halts the address at its hottest instant and asks the assembly to answer for exactly that moment: eyes that do not see, a wind gone still on the very spot, the shout still unpaid. The freeze lands as a demand on the hall: Shanhui Huan stops the address where a wedge is in the ear and sand in the eyes and rules the assembly blind and deaf in that moment; Poshan Haiming asks whether Deshan's staff and Linji's shout, the three catties of hemp and the dried shit-stick, can pass for the ghosts' and gods' tea and rice in it; Qianyan Yuanzhang asks how it is to be met — surpassing the herd is for the spirited hero, winning belongs to the lion's cub; Baiyu Jingsi lifts the whisk and asks whose affair it is in that moment, a jade hare in the moon bearing a phoenix. The rest keep the hinge and stock it differently: Mi'an Xianjie raises the old case of the woman who held the hermit fast and asked just at that moment what now, the answer a withered tree leaning on cold cliffs; Foyuan Chegang finds the wind still and the waves quiet in it and asks for the one line of a world at peace, Vimalakirti's palm hiding a world; Hansong Zhicao prices shaking off old Sakyamuni's snare as easy and letting the staff pass as hard; Tianyin Yuanxiu, each one's constant light standing forth, asks for the line that fits the hour — snow melting on the cliff, spring water swelling; Lanshi Ling verses that in it walking needs no steadying eye and sitting watches the stone tiger roar in the clouds; Dabian Xianquan sets the great work that does not govern aside and asks for the line that fully lifts the edict, sun and moon hung across the realm.
